cheatsheet.title: Connect keyless: Foundry SDK vs OpenAI v1 client
cheatsheet.code:
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider
from openai import OpenAI

# Foundry SDK: one project endpoint, Entra ID only
project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=PROJECT_ENDPOINT, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
openai = project.get_openai_client()
r1 = openai.responses.create(model="gpt-5-mini", instructions="Be concise.", input="Size of France?")
r2 = openai.responses.create(model="gpt-5-mini", input="And its capital?", previous_response_id=r1.id)
print(r2.output_text)

# OpenAI SDK on the v1 endpoint: no api-version, token auto-refresh
tp = get_bearer_token_provider(DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default")
client = OpenAI(base_url="https://YOUR-RESOURCE.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/", api_key=tp)
emb = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embedding-3-small", input="hello")
print(len(emb.data[0].embedding))
cheatsheet.note: `model` is always the deployment name, not the catalog model ID. Use `OpenAI`, not `AzureOpenAI`, on the v1 endpoint and pass the token provider callable itself as `api_key` to get automatic refresh. Exam era (Apr 2026): `azure-ai-projects` 2.0.x (GA March 6, 2026) and developer role Azure AI User on the project; the training module still shows the 1.x call `get_openai_client(api_version=...)`. Docs today: `azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0`, and the role is named Foundry User (since May 2026). Scope `https://ai.azure.com/.default` is in today's docs and the training module; older Azure OpenAI samples use `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default`. For a standalone Azure OpenAI resource the docs list Cognitive Services OpenAI User.

ref.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API

cheatsheet.title: Function-calling loop with the Responses API
cheatsheet.code:
tools = [{"type": "function", "name": "get_weather",
          "description": "Get weather for a location", "strict": True,
          "parameters": {"type": "object",
                         "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}},
                         "required": ["location"],
                         "additionalProperties": False}}]
resp = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, input=question, tools=tools)
outputs = []
for item in resp.output:
    if item.type == "function_call":
        args = json.loads(item.arguments)          # arguments is a JSON string
        outputs.append({"type": "function_call_output",
                        "call_id": item.call_id,   # must echo the call_id
                        "output": json.dumps(get_weather(**args))})
final = client.responses.create(model=MODEL, input=outputs,
                                previous_response_id=resp.id)
print(final.output_text)
cheatsheet.note: The model only requests the call; your app runs the function. Without `previous_response_id`, append `resp.output` (which holds the `function_call` items) to your input list before the `function_call_output` items. Strict mode needs every property in `required` and `additionalProperties: false`; structured outputs are not supported with parallel function calls, so set `parallel_tool_calls` to `false`.

ref.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API - Function calling

cheatsheet.title: Structured outputs: strict-mode rules and limits
bullets: Responses API: schema goes in `text.format`, with `type`, `name`, `schema`, and `strict` as sibling properties. Chat Completions: `response_format` with a nested `json_schema` object.
All fields must be listed in `required`. Emulate an optional field with a null union: `"type": ["string", "null"]`.
The root object cannot be `anyOf`. Nested `anyOf`, `$defs` / `$ref`, and recursive schemas are supported.
Limits: up to 100 object properties in total and up to 5 levels of nesting. Output keys follow the order of the schema.

Unsupported keywords: string `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `format`; number `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`; array `minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`, `contains`; object `patternProperties`, `minProperties`, `maxProperties`.
Function calling: add `"strict": true` to the function definition; not supported with parallel function calls.
JSON mode (`json_object`) guarantees valid JSON only - not adherence to your schema.

Python helpers: `client.responses.parse(..., text_format=PydanticModel)` -> `response.output_parsed`; Chat Completions uses `client.beta.chat.completions.parse(..., response_format=PydanticModel)` -> `message.parsed`.
cheatsheet.note: Supported types: String, Number, Boolean, Integer, Object, Array, Enum, anyOf. Structured outputs are not supported with `gpt-audio` / `gpt-audio-mini`.

cheatsheet.title: Responses API: state, streaming, background
rows: Works only for stored responses (default retention 30 days; `responses.delete(id)` removes one)
`inputs += response.output`, append the next user message, resend
History is re-sent and re-billed on every turn
`store=False` and pass back all output items, including reasoning items with `encrypted_content`
Mid-stream failures arrive as an `error` event while the HTTP status is 200
Requires `store=true`; resuming a stream needs `stream=True` on the original request (then pass `starting_after` with the last `sequence_number`)
Docs today; may postdate the April 2026 exam. The compaction item is opaque and encrypted; keep it in the next input
cheatsheet.note: Stream error types map to status codes: `server_error` 500, `too_many_requests` 429, `forbidden` 403, `user_error` 400. Code Interpreter containers expire after 20 minutes of inactivity and are billed per session.

cheatsheet.title: Evaluators: what they measure and what they need
rows: Response stays within the context, no fabrication (precision)
Strict consistency with context via Azure AI Content Safety
Retrieved chunks are relevant to the query
Nothing critical missing versus ground truth (recall)
Search quality: Fidelity, NDCG, XDCG, Max Relevance, Holes
Violence, Sexual, Self-Harm, Hate and Unfairness

cheatsheet.note: Direction trap: quality evaluators pass when score >= threshold (default 3); content-safety evaluators pass when severity <= threshold (default 3). Exam era (Apr 2026): the local SDK `azure-ai-evaluation` was in the main docs (docs today label that page classic): `GroundednessEvaluator(model_config)`, composites `QAEvaluator` and `ContentSafetyEvaluator`; safety evaluators and `GroundednessProEvaluator` take `azure_ai_project` instead of `model_config`; `evaluate(data=..., evaluators={...}, evaluator_config={...})` maps columns with `${data.context}`.

ref.title: Built-in evaluators reference

cheatsheet.title: Evaluate groundedness in code: local SDK and cloud evals API
cheatsheet.code:
# Exam-era local SDK: azure-ai-evaluation (labelled classic today)
groundedness = GroundednessEvaluator(model_config)   # judge = your GPT deployment
result = evaluate(data="data.jsonl",
    evaluators={"groundedness": groundedness},
    evaluator_config={"groundedness": {"column_mapping": {
        "context": "${data.context}", "response": "${data.response}"}}},
    azure_ai_project=azure_ai_project)               # optional: log to the project
# Cloud evaluation: Foundry SDK evals API
criteria = [{"type": "azure_ai_evaluator", "name": "groundedness",
             "evaluator_name": "builtin.groundedness",
             "initialization_parameters": {"deployment_name": judge},
             "data_mapping": {"context": "{{item.context}}",
                              "response": "{{item.response}}"}}]
ev = openai_client.evals.create(name="rag-eval",
    data_source_config=data_source_config, testing_criteria=criteria)
run = openai_client.evals.runs.create(eval_id=ev.id, name="run-1",
    data_source={"type": "jsonl", "source": {"type": "file_id", "id": data_id}})
run = openai_client.evals.runs.retrieve(run_id=run.id, eval_id=ev.id)  # poll
cheatsheet.note: Local SDK: `model_config` is an `AzureOpenAIModelConfiguration`; safety evaluators and `GroundednessProEvaluator` take `azure_ai_project` instead; the result has aggregate `metrics` and per-row `rows`. Cloud: `openai_client = project_client.get_openai_client()`; `data_id` comes from `project_client.datasets.upload_file(...)`; `{{item.x}}` = dataset column and `{{sample.output_text}}` = text generated by a model target; poll until `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`, then read `evals.runs.output_items.list(...)`. The cloud evals API has been in `azure-ai-projects` since the 2.0.0 beta releases (late 2025), so both paths are exam-era. The judge-model key appears as `deployment_name` on evaluator reference pages and as `model` in the dataset how-to. Role: Azure AI User on the project (named Foundry User today).

questions.stem: You are building a Python service for a Microsoft Foundry project. The service must enumerate the project's connections, start cloud evaluation runs that use the Foundry built-in evaluators, and call a `gpt-5-mini` deployment through the Responses API. Security policy requires Microsoft Entra ID authentication and prohibits API keys. You want to configure the service with a single endpoint. What should you use?
options: `OpenAI` client with `base_url` set to the resource's `/openai/v1/` endpoint and a bearer token provider
`AIProjectClient` with the project endpoint and `DefaultAzureCredential`, then `get_openai_client()` for model calls
`ChatCompletionsClient` from `azure-ai-inference` with the resource's `/models` endpoint and `DefaultAzureCredential`
questions.explanation: The Foundry SDK exposes two clients over one project endpoint: the project client for Foundry-native operations such as listing connections, and the OpenAI-compatible client from `get_openai_client()` for Responses and evaluations. The plain `OpenAI` client on `/openai/v1` is keyless-capable but has no project operations, and the docs say that endpoint does not provide Foundry-specific features such as agents and evaluations. `AzureOpenAI` and the Azure AI Inference `ChatCompletionsClient` target model endpoints only, so neither can enumerate project connections.

ref.title: Microsoft Foundry SDKs and endpoints

questions.stem: An ingestion job must create vectors by using a `text-embedding-3-small` deployment in a Microsoft Foundry resource. The job needs no other project features. The job must return one vector for each input chunk, must authenticate without keys, and must not manage `api-version` values. What should you use?
options: `AIProjectClient.get_openai_client()`, then `responses.create` with the embedding deployment name in `model`
`OpenAI` client on the `/openai/v1/` endpoint with a bearer token provider as `api_key`, then `embeddings.create`
`OpenAI` client on the `/openai/v1/` endpoint with the resource key as `api_key`, then `embeddings.create`
questions.explanation: The standard `OpenAI` client on the `/openai/v1` endpoint supports `embeddings.create`, needs no `api-version`, and accepts a Microsoft Entra token provider in `api_key`, so the job stays keyless. `AzureOpenAI` can also create embeddings but requires an `api_version`, the key-based variant breaks the keyless requirement, and the Responses API generates text, not vectors. Current-docs detail, not confirmed for the April 2026 exam era: the SDK overview recommends this endpoint for embeddings and warns that the project endpoint does not currently route embedding requests.

questions.stem: You are writing a Python app that connects to a Foundry project named `support-bot` in the Foundry resource `contoso-ai` and calls a model deployment by using the Responses API. Complete the code.
questions.code:
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

project = AIProjectClient(
    endpoint="https://contoso-ai.services.ai.azure.com/[[1]]",
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
)
openai = project.[[2]]()
response = openai.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5-mini",
    input="Summarize the open tickets.",
)
print(response.[[3]])
questions.explanation: The project endpoint has the form `https://YOUR-RESOURCE.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/YOUR-PROJECT`. `get_openai_client()` returns the OpenAI-compatible client for Responses, and the generated text is in `response.output_text`. `/openai/v1/` is the base URL for the plain `OpenAI` client, `choices[0].message.content` is the Chat Completions shape, and `content[0].text` is the Anthropic Messages shape.

questions.stem: You are migrating an app from the `AzureOpenAI` client to the Azure OpenAI v1 API. The app must not specify an `api-version`, must authenticate by using a managed identity, and must refresh tokens automatically. Complete the code.
questions.code:
import openai
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider

token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(
    DefaultAzureCredential(), "https://ai.azure.com/.default"
)
client = openai.[[1]](
    base_url="https://contoso-ai.openai.azure.com/[[2]]",
    [[3]]=token_provider,
)
response = client.responses.create(model="gpt-5-mini", input="Hello")
print(response.output_text)
questions.explanation: With the v1 API you use the standard `OpenAI` client, set `base_url` to the resource endpoint with `/openai/v1/` appended, and omit `api-version`; the dated pre-v1 routes are the ones that need an API version. Passing the token provider callable as `api_key` gives automatic token retrieval and refresh, whereas `azure_ad_token_provider` belongs to the `AzureOpenAI` client. Scope note: today's docs and the training module use `https://ai.azure.com/.default`, while older Azure OpenAI samples use `https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default`, so accept whichever an exam item offers.

questions.stem: A chat app calls `client.responses.create` once per user turn. Follow-up questions such as "And what about last year?" are answered without any context. You need the service to carry the context forward between turns. The solution must not resend earlier turns from the client and must require the least code. What should you do?
options: Append `response.output` to a list and pass the whole list as `input` on every call
Set `store=False` and add `reasoning.encrypted_content` to the `include` parameter
Set `background=True` and call `responses.retrieve` before each new turn
Pass the `id` of the last response in the `previous_response_id` parameter
questions.explanation: The Responses API is stateful: passing the previous response ID in `previous_response_id` chains the new turn to the stored context, so the client sends only the new input. Manually appending `response.output` also works but resends the history on every call. `store=False` makes requests stateless, which is the opposite of the goal, and background mode is for long-running asynchronous tasks.

ref.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API - Chaining responses together

questions.stem: A compliance team requires a chat app that uses a reasoning model to send every Responses API request with `store=False`, so that the service does not persist conversation state. You review the impact on the app design. For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.text: The app can continue a conversation by passing `previous_response_id` from the previous turn.
To preserve the model's reasoning context, the app must keep the returned output items, including reasoning items that contain `encrypted_content`, and send them in `input` on the next turn.
The app can submit long-running requests by setting `background=True`.

questions.explanation: The docs say not to use `previous_response_id` for an unstored response; in stateless mode the application supplies the context on every request. Prior messages alone do not carry the model's reasoning, so you replay the returned items, including the encrypted reasoning items, in their original order. Background mode requires `store=true`; stateless requests are not supported.

ref.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API - Encrypted reasoning

questions.stem: You are implementing function calling with the Responses API. The model has returned a response that asks the app to run the local `get_order_status` function. Complete the code that returns the function result to the model.
questions.explanation: In the Responses API a function request is an output item with `type` equal to `function_call` that carries `name`, `arguments` (a JSON string), and `call_id`. The app runs the function and sends back an item of type `function_call_output` with the same `call_id`. `tool_calls`, the `tool` role, and `tool_call_id` are the Chat Completions equivalents and are not valid here.

ref.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API - Function calling

questions.stem: You are porting an app from `chat.completions.create` to `responses.create`. The existing tool definition is shown. After the port, the request is rejected because the tool definition is invalid. Strict schema adherence for the function arguments must be kept. What should you change?
options: Rename `parameters` to `input_schema` and leave the `function` wrapper in place
Remove `additionalProperties` from `parameters` because strict mode rejects it
Remove the `function` wrapper and move its properties up, next to `type`
Replace `"strict": true` with `"parallel_tool_calls": false` inside the `function` object
questions.explanation: Function tools in the Responses API use a flat definition: `type`, `name`, `description`, `parameters`, and `strict` sit at the top level of the tool object. Chat Completions nests the same fields under `function`, which is why the ported definition fails. `additionalProperties: false` is required for strict mode rather than rejected, the schema stays in `parameters`, and `parallel_tool_calls` is a request-level parameter, not part of a tool definition.

questions.stem: You are calling the Responses API through REST to extract invoice data. The output must always conform to a JSON Schema. The `po_number` value might be missing from an invoice, and in that case the model must return `null` for it. Complete the request body.
questions.explanation: The Responses API takes the schema in `text.format`, with `type` set to `json_schema` and `name`, `schema`, and `strict` as siblings; `response_format` is the Chat Completions parameter. Strict mode requires every field to appear in `required`, so an optional value is modeled with a null union and still listed. `json_object` is JSON mode, which guarantees valid JSON but not adherence to the schema.

ref.title: Structured outputs

questions.stem: A Python service uses the Responses API on the Azure OpenAI v1 endpoint to extract meeting details from email text. You define a Pydantic model named `CalendarEvent`. The model output must be guaranteed to match the schema, and the SDK must return a populated `CalendarEvent` instance without custom JSON parsing code. Which call should you use?
questions.explanation: For the Responses API, `responses.parse` accepts a Pydantic model in `text_format`, converts it to a JSON Schema under `text.format`, and returns the typed object in `output_parsed`. `response_format` is the Chat Completions parameter, and the Chat Completions helper takes `response_format`, not `text_format`. JSON mode (`json_object`) only guarantees syntactically valid JSON and still needs manual parsing.
